business_problem: Minijob-Zentrale needed a faster way to turn complex regulatory updates into clear, audience-appropriate articles without forcing editors to spend most of their time on repetitive research and rewriting.
solution_summary: Minijob-Zentrale worked with IBM Client Engineering and IBM iX within IBM Consulting to design 'Mini,' a generative-AI editorial assistant built on IBM watsonx.ai. IBM first analyzed MJZ's editorial workflow, co-created wireframes, and defined the product vision before technical buildout. In the prototype, watsonx.ai helps editors generate ideas, simplify dense regulatory language, adapt drafts for different audience segments, and suggest keywords after reviewing previously published content. The assistant is positioned as a workflow augmentation layer rather than an autonomous publisher: editors keep full control, while the model removes repetitive research and rewriting steps that slow article production. By inserting AI into planning, drafting, and audience adaptation, MJZ turned a complex public-information publishing process into a faster, more creative, and more empathetic content workflow.
